title: Setting prices in bulk
summary: Supermarket Simulator gives you pricing decisions well beyond one item at a time: the game has bulk pricing panels and their own section types, plus a separate discount system.
body: Pricing is organised in bulk rather than per item on the shelf: the game has a bulk pricing manager and a panel for it, which is where you set prices for groups of goods.
Sections of the bulk pricing panel are typed, so the panel can present different kinds of price decisions in the same place.
Discounts are handled separately from prices, so a discount is not the same thing as changing a price.
What this entry does not tell you: the exact price steps, how many products a section covers, or how discounts affect customer behaviour. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Prices can be set in bulk through a dedicated manager and panel.
The bulk pricing panel is built from typed sections.
Discounts are a separate system from prices.
The price tag a bulk price is written on is an object the build ships.
Barcodes are things the build makes: it names a creator for them, a spawner and a sticker decal for one.
facts.evidence: asset names: BarcodeCreator, Barcode Spawner, M_Barcode_Sticker_Decal

facts.claim: The shop's scanner is named in the build, with a colour sheet of its own.
Bulk pricing has a wholesale offer of its own, with a toggle that enables it and a key entry beside it.
facts.evidence: asset names: Wholesale Offer, EnableWholeSale, EnableWholeSaleToggle, KeybindEntry_Wholesale

facts.claim: The discount side is named piece by piece: a section, a button with text on it, a line and a discounted price.
facts.evidence: asset names: Discount Section, DiscountButton, DiscountButtonText, DiscountLine, DiscountedPrice

facts.claim: The pricing interface is named piece by piece: a price input, a quick-pick element and separate total and unit price texts.
facts.evidence: asset names: Price Input, Price Quick Pick Element, Total Price Text, Unit Price Text
